I do not understand your question - please restate it. Thunderbird doesn't "want" responses. I don't know what Java bug you're referring to. Thunderbird is merely the agent that sends messages to your email service and they take care of sending it on to the recipient. It also relays responses such as non-delivery notices from your email service to you - it does not generate them.

If you see any error messages, please quote them precisely and in full. Screen shots would suffice.

The message was not sent due to exceeding the allowed number of recipients.

This is your email provider's server complaining about the no. of recipients you're sending a message to, not the no. of messages. It has got nothing to do with Thunderbird. If you're sending messages to a larger no. of recipients create a mailing list. https://support.mozilla.org/kb/how-create-and-use-mailing-lists-thunderbird

I have managed to send emails from the website of my email provider that I haven't been able to send through Thunderbird. This suggests that the previous answer was wrong.

You're drawing the wrong conclusion. Webmail is an entirely different server infrastructure than POP/IMAP/SMTP servers. Webmail may impose different sending limits compared to SMTP servers. If in doubt, check with your email provider what those limits are.

content:
If incoming mail is working, I’d look at the outgoing SMTP settings first. Thunderbird uses a separate server for sending, and sometimes an update, password change or provider change can mess with that connection.

Go to Account Settings > Outgoing Server (SMTP) and check that the server name, port, security setting and username match what your email provider recommends. Also make sure the username is the full email address if your provider requires it. Don’t guess the settings, check the provider’s support page. Thunderbird Help

If you have more than one email account, make sure each account is linked to the correct SMTP server. I’d also check whether your antivirus, VPN or firewall is blocking outgoing mail. Before changing too much, post the exact error message and tell us who your email provider is. That’ll usually point straight at the problem.

  2. Compattare le cartelle -> https://support.mozilla.org/it/kb/compattazione-cartelle
  3. Riavviare Thunderbird
  4. Se il problema non è risolto, ricostruire l'indice globale -> https://support.mozilla.org/it/kb/ricostruzione-indice-globale
  5. Riavviare Thunderbird
